title: 9 Insanely Cheap AI Stocks to Buy Now
creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
summary: Joseph Hogue ranks 60 AI stocks by growth-adjusted price-to-sales and free cash flow to find the nine cheapest after a month-long AI sell-off that took the Nasdaq into correction, worsened by midterm election fears over data-centre opposition. His thesis is that nothing fundamental changed: the four hyperscalers plus Oracle are set to invest over $1tn in AI next year, with $2.3tn of data-centre projects in development. The nine: Astera Labs (39% upside at 23x sales, 137% revenue growth), Nvidia (83% upside at 20x sales on $411bn revenue, $127bn free cash flow), Oracle (26% upside but hesitant, -$28bn free cash flow), Teradyne (50% upside, 138% earnings growth), Upstart (62% upside but cheap for a reason, -$35m free cash flow), HPE (only ~17% upside, hesitant), Micron (146% upside at 7x sales, $58bn free cash flow), Dell (~18% upside) and Super Micro (146% upside at 0.6x sales, but management scandals and -$6.9bn free cash flow). He also re-ranks by price-to-free-cash-flow, flagging Adobe and Salesforce as cheap but facing AI demand destruction, and Micron as cheap despite memory cyclicality. His method section explains the spreadsheet: market cap from Yahoo Finance, free cash flow from cash-flow statements, and price-to-sales adjusted for expected revenue growth. Caption garbles: Oracle appears as 'OCL', Teradyne as 'Pterodine', Upstart's ticker as 'UPS'.

calls.video_title: 9 Insanely Cheap AI Stocks to Buy Now
calls.thesis: Long-time favourite in AI networking connectivity: revenue expected +125-137% to ~$2bn this year; at 23x price-to-sales (its low over the past year) fair value is ~$46bn market cap vs $33.2bn now, about 39% upside.
calls.base_case: Investors return to the AI theme and pay 23x sales on $2bn revenue for ~39% upside.
calls.bull_case: Analyst estimates keep being raised (124% to 137% growth in days) and the multiple re-rates toward its June peak of 86x sales.
calls.bear_case: Price-to-sales stays compressed on AI-bust fears and the growth forecast disappoints.

calls.video_title: 9 Insanely Cheap AI Stocks to Buy Now
calls.thesis: Stance flips from UNCERTAIN (9 Nov): 83% upside if Nvidia returns to a still-conservative 20x price-to-sales on $411bn expected revenue (+90% this year, +68% next); $127bn free cash flow (3.5x P/FCF) and he does not think Jensen will be forced out over the affair.
calls.base_case: At 20x sales on $411bn revenue the stock is worth ~$8.2tn vs $4.5tn now (+83%).
calls.bull_case: Revenue reaches ~$700bn next year and the multiple recovers toward 22-25x sales.
calls.bear_case: Custom-chip competition (Broadcom, Marvell, AMD), hyperscaler spending cuts and export restrictions slow growth.

calls.video_title: 9 Insanely Cheap AI Stocks to Buy Now
calls.thesis: First tracked Teradyne call: 50% upside to 10x price-to-sales on $5.2bn revenue (+64% this year); 138% earnings growth as chip complexity lifts semiconductor test equipment demand, plus industrial robotics.
calls.base_case: At 10x sales on $5.2bn revenue, a $52bn market cap vs $34.6bn now (+50%).
calls.bull_case: Multiple returns toward the 20x sales seen in June for far larger upside.
calls.bear_case: Revenue growth slows to 24% next year and the AI fear premium persists.
calls.price_at_call: $34bn market cap (~$240/share, down from a ~$500 peak)

calls.video_title: 9 Insanely Cheap AI Stocks to Buy Now
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated: 'put this on your list of stocks to look at maybe stocks to buy' — 146% upside even at a conservative 7x price-to-sales on $275bn revenue (+107% this year); $58bn free cash flow and one of only three global DRAM makers.
calls.base_case: At 7x sales on $275bn revenue, ~146% upside to a ~$2tn market cap.
calls.bull_case: At 10x sales the upside is ~252%; memory shortage keeps prices and margins high.
calls.bear_case: Memory cyclicality returns: revenue growth hits a wall at 16% next year and overproduction kills pricing.

calls.video_title: 9 Insanely Cheap AI Stocks to Buy Now
calls.thesis: Stance flips from HOLD (2 Nov): cheapest name on the list at 0.24x price-to-sales with 146% upside at 0.6x sales on $77.6bn revenue (+98%); makes the best high-performance servers of the three server makers — but management scandals and -$6.9bn free cash flow are the reason it is cheap.
calls.base_case: At 0.6x sales on $77.6bn revenue, ~146% upside to a $46.5bn market cap.
calls.bull_case: Management stays out of the way, data-centre spend continues and the multiple reaches 0.7x sales or more.
calls.bear_case: Another management scandal or the revenue wall (11% growth next year) keeps investors away.
